# Moodle CLI 0.9.0

`moodle submit UNIT "TASK" report.pdf` uploads files into an assignment. The command
shows a plan first: what is uploaded, in bold, and where it lands, in cyan, on
separate lines, then asks before anything is sent. Uploads run under a spinner
that names each file as it goes, and the receipt reports what Moodle recorded.
Local MCP servers expose the same action as their only write tool.

## Working at a terminal

Bare `moodle`, `edstem` and `ontrack` now open the same styled help: a wordmark,
the description, commands grouped the way `gh` groups them (core, additional,
agent), cyan flags, and a short "Try" list. Every subcommand page follows the
same shape.

A missing unit, task or file becomes a picker or a prompt instead of a usage
error. An ambiguous match is chosen from a list. On the first run with no
session, the CLI walks through the site address and browser sign-in once and
remembers it. All of this only happens at a terminal: a pipe, `--json` or an
agent's shell still gets the plain error with the usage line in its hint.

Tables paint the first column as the key and tone status-like words (`overdue`,
`submitted`, `graded`, `announcement`) so a row can be scanned by colour.
`--no-color` and `NO_COLOR` turn every escape code off; files and pipes never
carry them.

## Other changes

Per-command output flags are hidden from help pages; the root names them once.
Commands carry short summaries in listings, and `find` documents its arguments.
